title: Benefits Verification Bulletin: Dating a Regimen Change From the Testing-Supplies Record for Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Renewals
content:
Under the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, the regimen change date that applies to a renewal written order for the CGM supply allowance (HCPCS A4239) is read from the customer's Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program at Larkfield Medical Supply: its documented treatment class, the date it was activated, and the order dates of its written orders.

**Clause.** The regimen-change adjustment replaces the standard regimen change date from the customer's testing-supplies record: when the customer's testing-supplies program documents non-insulin treatment and has a written order on file, the regimen change date is that program's newest written order date; when it documents non-insulin treatment with no written order on file, it is the date that program was activated; otherwise the standard regimen change date applies.

**Reading the records.**

| Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program documents non-insulin treatment | Written order on file on that program | Regimen change date |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the order date of that program's newest written order |
| yes | no | the date that program was activated |
| no (insulin-treated diabetes documented, or no testing-supplies program held) | any | the standard regimen change date |

"Non-insulin treatment" is the treatment class "non-insulin treated" on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program. The newest written order is the one with the latest order date.

**Examples (hypothetical dates).**

- The Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program documents non-insulin treatment and holds written orders dated 5 May and 12 September of a hypothetical Year 1. The regimen change date is 12 September of Year 1.
- The same program documents non-insulin treatment, was activated on 20 January of Year 1, and holds no written order. The regimen change date is 20 January of Year 1.
- The testing-supplies program documents insulin-treated diabetes. The standard regimen change date applies, whatever its written orders show.
